title: what-happens-when-you-read-every-day
style: minimalist 2D line-art cartoon, thin ink outlines, flat muted pastel fills, soft shadows, high-key lighting, clean white background, educational animation style

characters.prompt: Character reference sheet: young Black man in his early 20s wearing 1940s denim prison uniform, short hair, thoughtful intense expression — front view, side view, three expressions (focused, weary, quietly triumphant)
Character reference sheet: young person in their 20s with long dark hair, grey t-shirt and jeans — front view, side view, three expressions (bored, curious, delighted)

scenes.label: Hook
scenes.vo: Reading is to the mind what exercise is to the body, wrote Joseph Addison, in seventeen eleven.
scenes.prompt: Elegant serif quotation text centered on a clean white card, small minimalist book logo beneath, static title card
scenes.motion: static title card, gentle fade in

scenes.label: Hook
scenes.vo: While most people dread a prison sentence, one young inmate in 1946 found something unexpected behind bars: his university.
scenes.prompt: 1940s prison cell interior, young man in denim prison uniform sitting on a bunk holding an open book that glows faintly, moonlight through barred window, muted blue-grey palette

scenes.label: Hook
scenes.vo: Frustrated that he couldn't express himself in letters, Malcolm Little set himself an impossible task: copying out the entire dictionary, page by page.
scenes.prompt: Man at tiny prison desk copying from an enormous dictionary, handwritten pages piling up around him in drifts like snow, warm lamplight

scenes.label: Hook
scenes.vo: From there he devoured history, philosophy, science — reading in the library, in his bunk, in every spare minute.
scenes.prompt: Three-panel montage: man reading in a prison library aisle, reading cross-legged on a bunk, reading at a mess hall table, warm muted tones

scenes.label: Hook
scenes.vo: But the prison had one strict rule: lights out at ten. And Malcolm was never ready to stop.
scenes.prompt: Close-up of man's face in near darkness lit by a thin strip of corridor light, guard silhouette approaching in background hallway, high contrast, suspenseful

scenes.label: Bridge
scenes.vo: Few of us will ever read with that kind of hunger. But research suggests even a modest daily reading habit can measurably change your brain.
scenes.prompt: Young person slouched on couch scrolling phone, dusty unread book on coffee table, cool desaturated tones, question mark thought bubble forming

scenes.label: Mechanism
scenes.vo: The effects begin within minutes. In one widely cited study, just six minutes of reading reduced stress levels by more than two-thirds.
scenes.prompt: Young person opening a book on a couch, jagged red scribble above their head transforming into a smooth calm blue wave, shoulders relaxing

scenes.label: Mechanism
scenes.vo: As your eyes track the words, a network of brain regions lights up together — decoding symbols, conjuring images, simulating the story as if you were living it.
scenes.prompt: Side profile of young person reading, glowing blue circles over brain regions, tiny imagined scenes of a ship and a storm floating above the open book
scenes.motion: circles pulse gently, imagined scenes drift upward

scenes.label: Mechanism
scenes.vo: Reading fiction in particular is thought to exercise theory of mind — your ability to model what other people think and feel.
scenes.prompt: Young person reading while translucent story characters — a knight, an elderly woman, a child — step out of the book, oversized empty shoes lined up on the floor
scenes.motion: ghostly characters step out of the pages

scenes.label: Mechanism
scenes.vo: Within weeks, the habit leaves physical traces. One study found reading a novel increased connectivity in the brain's language cortex — changes that lingered for days.
scenes.prompt: Stylized brain drawn as a city road map at night, new glowing routes lighting up and staying lit, book pages turning in the foreground corner
scenes.motion: roads light up one by one

scenes.label: Mechanism
scenes.vo: Every new word you meet gets filed away — and readers encounter far more rare words in print than in everyday conversation.
scenes.prompt: Cute personified brain character wearing a librarian cardigan, stamping word cards and filing them into a towering card catalog, warm yellows

scenes.label: Mechanism
scenes.vo: Sustained reading also trains something increasingly rare: deep, unbroken attention. Like a muscle, focus strengthens with use.
scenes.prompt: Young person reading inside a glowing protective bubble at a desk, notification bell icons bouncing off the bubble like insects

scenes.label: Mechanism
scenes.vo: And over decades the payoff compounds. Research links lifelong reading to slower memory decline in old age — building what scientists call cognitive reserve.
scenes.prompt: Elderly man reading in an armchair, bookshelf behind him stacking like fortress bricks into a protective wall around the silhouette of a head, earthy warm tones

scenes.label: Mechanism
scenes.vo: Simply put, reading is exercise for your brain. No equipment, no membership, no minimum fitness level. A library card will do.
scenes.prompt: Young person walking past gym equipment — dumbbells, treadmill, yoga mats — picking up a small glowing golden library card

scenes.label: Application
scenes.vo: And forget the guilt of unfinished reading challenges. Studies suggest any increase in reading time yields benefits. A chapter counts. A page counts.
scenes.prompt: Giant cracked trophy labeled 52 toppling over, young person calmly picking up one glowing page from the debris, playful tone

scenes.label: Application
scenes.vo: Minutes hide everywhere: an audiobook on the commute, a chapter with morning coffee, a few pages in a waiting line.
scenes.prompt: Three-panel montage: person with headphones on a bus, person reading with steaming coffee at sunrise, person reading an e-reader in a queue, pastel palette

scenes.label: Application
scenes.vo: In communities rich with libraries, bookstores, and little reading nooks, those minutes accumulate almost effortlessly.
scenes.prompt: Vibrant pastel city street with sidewalk book stalls, sunlit library, children reading under a leafy tree, cozy book cafe, the most colorful saturated scene, young person strolling with a book under their arm
scenes.motion: slow lateral tracking through the street

scenes.label: Application
scenes.vo: Reading before bed, reading to your kids, reading with friends — each has its own ripple effects.
scenes.prompt: Split screen three panels: person reading in bed by warm lamplight, parent reading a picture book to a delighted toddler, cozy book club laughing around a table with a dog, warm lighting
scenes.motion: panels slide in one by one

scenes.label: Application
scenes.vo: Children read to daily may hear over a million more words by age five. And one study found adults in shared reading groups felt measurably less lonely.
scenes.prompt: Words spiraling from an open bedtime storybook into a small galaxy above a child's head, people below connected by warm glowing threads, saturated warm colors

scenes.label: Obstacle
scenes.vo: So why doesn't everyone just read more? For one, our attention has never been under heavier siege.
scenes.prompt: Young person opening a book while a grey tornado of notification icons swirls around them, glowing phone pulling their gaze, desaturated grey palette

scenes.label: Obstacle
scenes.vo: In the United States, the share of people who read for pleasure on a given day has fallen by roughly a third since the early two-thousands.
scenes.prompt: Staircase built of stacked books descending like a declining bar chart, small figure standing at the bottom looking up, harsh grey lighting, high contrast

scenes.label: Obstacle
scenes.vo: Meanwhile many communities have become book deserts, as library budgets shrink and local bookstores close.
scenes.prompt: Officials in suits wheeling a giant piggy bank away from a public library going dark window by window, bookstore with a swinging CLOSED sign, cool grey palette
scenes.motion: library windows go dark one by one

scenes.label: Obstacle
scenes.vo: In some neighborhoods, researchers counted just one age-appropriate book for every three hundred children.
scenes.prompt: Desert landscape where sand dunes are shaped like giant closed books, one child holding a single small book, crowd of child silhouettes stretching to the horizon

scenes.label: Fixes
scenes.vo: But there are ways to rebuild a reading culture. In 2009 a Wisconsin man filled a tiny model schoolhouse with books and put it on a post in his yard.
scenes.prompt: A small wooden book-box on a post on a suburban lawn, a man stepping back proudly, neighbors approaching curiously, hopeful warm light
scenes.motion: gentle push-in on the little library

scenes.label: Fixes
scenes.vo: Today more than a hundred thousand of these Little Free Libraries stand in over a hundred countries.
scenes.prompt: Aerial view of a world map as tiny wooden book boxes multiply across it in a chain reaction of spreading warm lights, time-lapse feel
scenes.motion: speed-ramp time lapse of lights spreading

scenes.label: Fixes
scenes.vo: And small personal measures help too: a book on the pillow instead of a phone on the nightstand. Habit researchers call it making the good choice the easy one.
scenes.prompt: Grey bedroom blooming into warm color as a young person places a book on the pillow while the phone charges away in a drawer, cozy reading chair glowing by the window

scenes.label: Bookend
scenes.vo: As for Malcolm — when the lights went out he moved to the floor by his cell door and kept reading in the corridor's glow, dodging the guards' patrols until dawn.
scenes.prompt: Man reading on a prison cell floor in a wedge of golden corridor light, serene focused expression, deep shadows elsewhere, golden hour palette

scenes.label: Bookend
scenes.vo: He entered prison with an eighth-grade education. He left as one of the century's most electrifying voices — later writing that he had never been so truly free.
scenes.prompt: Man walking out of open prison gates into a sunrise holding a book, waving back, long warm shadows, golden hour palette

scenes.label: CTA
scenes.vo: You don't have to copy out a dictionary to change your brain. Tonight, one page is enough to begin.
scenes.prompt: Parade of all characters walking across a clean white frame each holding a book — man in denim, young person, parent with toddler, elderly man, cute brain character, a dog
scenes.motion: characters stroll across frame left to right

scenes.label: CTA
scenes.vo: So pick the book you've been meaning to read — and give your brain its daily walk.
scenes.prompt: Minimalist end card with centered text READ ONE PAGE TONIGHT, small credit lines, characters walking faintly in the background, static final frame
